name: stall-alarm
description: Raises the alarm when a long-running session stalls while you are away: a permission dialog or a question that has waited for you past a threshold (toast, Mac notification, optional phone push, repeated while it stays open), and a turn that stopped on a login, usage-limit or billing error, with the fix. Leaves scheduled routines to routine-watch. No model calls.

stallMinutes.title: Minutes before a wait is a stall
stallMinutes.description: How long a permission dialog or an AskUserQuestion may wait for you before the alarm fires. The status line shows the wait from then on.

repeatMinutes.title: Minutes between repeat alarms for a permission dialog
repeatMinutes.description: While the same permission dialog stays open, alarm again this often: it blocks a goal. 0: alarm once per dialog.

questionRepeatMinutes.title: Minutes between repeat alarms for a question
questionRepeatMinutes.description: While the same AskUserQuestion stays open, alarm again this often: less often than a dialog, since nothing runs while a question waits. 0: alarm once per question.

questionRepeats.title: Repeat alarms per question
questionRepeats.description: How many times at most a question alarms again after its first alarm; then it stays open quietly, still on the status line. 0: alarm once, never repeat.

notifyMac.title: Mac notification
notifyMac.description: Post a macOS notification (osascript, with a sound) on each alarm, beside the toast.

notifyCommand.title: Phone push command
notifyCommand.description: Also run this command on each alarm, e.g. curl -s -d {message} ntfy.sh/my-topic. It is split on spaces and {title} and {message} are filled into single arguments; no shell is involved. Empty: no push.

alarmOnAnyError.title: Alarm on any error
alarmOnAnyError.description: Alarm when a turn ends on any error. Off: only login, usage-limit, rate-limit, billing and overload errors alarm.

skipRoutines.title: Leave routines to routine-watch
skipRoutines.description: Stay quiet in scheduled-task (routine) sessions, which routine-watch already watches, so one stall does not alarm twice.
